summary: Modern databases and data platforms have rapidly embedded AI/ML capabilities directly into their query engines, eliminating the need to move data to external systems for inference and model training. Vector search has become a foundational primitive across platforms, with 75% of enterprise AI applications expected to depend on vector search by 2026 and adoption growing 377% year over year. The competitive landscape now spans purpose-built vector databases, Postgres extensions like pgvector, and fully integrated cloud data platforms offering LLM connectivity, embedding generation, and AutoML within familiar SQL interfaces.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex AI provides a suite of serverless AI functions accessible via SQL, including LLM inference (Cortex Complete), text embedding generation (Cortex Embed), text-to-SQL (Cortex Analyst), document processing (Cortex Search), and fine-tuning capabilities. As of early 2026, Snowflake Postgres runs natively in the AI Data Cloud and integrates with pgvector for vector similarity search, with Cortex providing embedding generation and text-to-SQL directly within Postgres workflows. Cortex Guard adds safety filtering for LLM outputs.
databases.vector_search_notes: Snowflake has native vector search via Cortex Search, which supports hybrid search (semantic + keyword) over unstructured data. Additionally, Snowflake Postgres integrates with pgvector for vector similarity search within Postgres instances running natively in the AI Data Cloud. VECTOR data type is supported natively in Snowflake tables with VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY and related functions.
databases.llm_integration: Supports hosted models including Llama 3.x, Mistral, Reka, Jamba, and Arctic (Snowflake's own LLM) via Cortex Complete. Models run inside Snowflake's security perimeter with no data leaving the platform. Supports bring-your-own-model via Snowpark Container Services.
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed in Snowflake credits. Embedding generation, LLM inference, and Cortex Search each consume credits at different rates depending on model size and token volume. Cortex Search has additional storage costs for indexes. Snowflake Postgres pricing announced as generally available soon as of February 2026.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML and Vertex AI Integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data analysts to create and execute ML models directly in BigQuery using SQL. Supported model types include logistic regression, linear regression, k-means clustering, matrix factorization, time series forecasting (ARIMA+), boosted trees (XGBoost), DNNs, and AutoML Tables. BigQuery also integrates deeply with Vertex AI, enabling remote model invocation via ML.PREDICT, embedding generation via ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, and generative text via ML.GENERATE_TEXT against Gemini and other Vertex-hosted models. The VECTOR_SEARCH function provides native approximate nearest neighbor search over embedding columns.
databases.vector_search_notes: BigQuery has a native VECTOR_SEARCH function (generally available) that performs approximate nearest neighbor search using embeddings stored directly in BigQuery tables. No external extension or separate infrastructure is required. Supports cosine, Euclidean, and dot product distance metrics.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates natively with Google Vertex AI, providing access to Gemini 1.5 Pro/Flash, text-embedding models, and other Vertex-hosted models via SQL functions ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING. Supports external model endpoints and Vertex AI Model Garden.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML model training and prediction consume BigQuery compute (slot hours or on-demand query pricing). Calls to Vertex AI models via BigQuery incur additional Vertex AI API charges billed separately. VECTOR_SEARCH queries are billed as standard BigQuery queries based on bytes processed.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: PostgreSQL itself has no built-in AI/ML capabilities, but the open-source extension ecosystem provides powerful options. pgvector adds a VECTOR data type and vector similarity search operators (cosine, inner product, L2 distance) to any Postgres instance, with HNSW and IVFFlat indexing for approximate nearest neighbor search. pgai (by Timescale) extends this further with SQL functions for calling OpenAI, Cohere, Ollama, and other LLM APIs directly from Postgres, and pgvectorscale adds DiskANN indexing for improved performance at scale. These extensions require no new infrastructure and use the same security model and backup procedures as Postgres.
databases.vector_search_notes: PostgreSQL does not have native built-in vector search. Vector search is provided by the third-party open-source extension pgvector, which must be installed separately. When pgvector is installed, it adds full vector similarity search including HNSW and IVFFlat indexing. Managed Postgres services (AWS RDS, Supabase, Neon, Snowflake Postgres) typically offer pgvector as a supported extension. Per the research, pgvector is described as a Postgres extension rather than a database in its own right.
databases.llm_integration: pgai extension enables direct SQL-based calls to OpenAI (GPT-4o, embeddings), Anthropic Claude, Cohere, and Ollama (local models). Timescale's pgai Vectorizer automates embedding generation and synchronization. No native LLM integration in vanilla PostgreSQL without extensions.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are open-source and free to use. Costs are determined by the underlying Postgres hosting (self-managed, RDS, Supabase, Neon, etc.) plus any external LLM API costs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) incurred by pgai function calls.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.description: Amazon Aurora ML integrates Aurora (MySQL-compatible and PostgreSQL-compatible editions) with external AWS ML services, primarily Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Comprehend, via native SQL functions. Users can call SageMaker-hosted model endpoints for inference or use Comprehend for sentiment analysis and entity detection directly from SQL queries without moving data outside Aurora. Aurora PostgreSQL also supports the pgvector extension for vector similarity search, though this is an extension rather than a native Aurora capability.
databases.vector_search_notes: Aurora does not have native built-in vector search. Aurora PostgreSQL supports vector search via the pgvector open-source extension, which must be enabled. Aurora MySQL does not support pgvector. Since vector search depends on a third-party extension rather than native Aurora functionality, vector_search is marked false.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon SageMaker for custom and hosted model inference via the aws_ml.invoke_endpoint() SQL function. Integrates with Amazon Comprehend for NLP tasks (sentiment, key phrases, entities, language detection) via aws_comprehend SQL functions. Does not natively integrate with Amazon Bedrock LLMs directly through SQL as of mid-2026; Bedrock calls require application-layer code or Lambda intermediaries.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML itself does not add a separate charge — standard Aurora instance and I/O pricing applies. However, SageMaker endpoint inference and Amazon Comprehend API calls are billed separately at their respective AWS service rates. Data transfer between Aurora and SageMaker in the same region is typically free.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.description: Amazon Redshift ML allows users to create, train, and invoke ML models using SQL statements directly within Redshift, powered by Amazon SageMaker Autopilot under the hood. Using CREATE MODEL SQL syntax, Redshift ML automatically trains a model using SageMaker Autopilot (handling feature engineering, algorithm selection, and hyperparameter tuning), then deploys it for in-database inference via a SQL function. Supported problem types include binary classification, multiclass classification, regression, and k-means clustering. Models trained externally in SageMaker can also be imported for inference.
databases.vector_search_notes: Redshift does not support native vector search or the pgvector extension. Redshift is a columnar analytical data warehouse and has no VECTOR data type or ANN index capability. Workloads requiring vector search alongside Redshift data typically require exporting embeddings to a separate vector database or using Redshift with an external integration.
databases.llm_integration: Redshift ML integrates with Amazon SageMaker for AutoML model training and inference. As of 2025-2026, AWS has added support for invoking Amazon Bedrock foundation models (including Claude and Amazon Titan) from Redshift via the ML.PREDICT function and Bedrock integration, enabling generative AI and text embedding use cases within SQL workflows.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift ML incurs SageMaker Autopilot training costs (billed by SageMaker instance hours during training), S3 storage costs for model artifacts, and SageMaker endpoint costs for inference hosting. The Redshift cluster itself is billed separately. Using Bedrock models adds Bedrock API invocation costs.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI is a comprehensive AI development platform built on the Databricks Lakehouse, encompassing model training, fine-tuning, serving, evaluation, and agent orchestration. Key capabilities include Mosaic AI Model Training for large-scale distributed training and fine-tuning of foundation models, Model Serving for low-latency inference endpoints, AI Playground for interactive LLM testing, and MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry. Databricks Vector Search provides a serverless vector database built into the Lakehouse, with automatic sync from Delta Lake tables. The platform also includes Agent Framework for building and evaluating LLM agents and RAG pipelines.
databases.vector_search_notes: Databricks Vector Search is a native, fully managed vector database integrated into the Databricks platform. It supports automatic synchronization of embeddings from Delta Lake tables, real-time and batch indexing, and similarity search with metadata filtering. No separate infrastructure is required. Supports cosine and dot product similarity with managed HNSW-style indexes. The research notes pgvector integrates well with Databricks as an alternative path.
databases.llm_integration: Supports a broad range of LLMs via Model Serving, including Meta Llama 3.x, Mistral, DBRX (Databricks' own LLM), and external APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini) via AI Gateway (Mosaic AI Gateway). Embedding models from Hugging Face and custom fine-tuned models are natively supported. Foundation Model APIs provide pay-per-token access to curated hosted models.
databases.pricing_notes: Mosaic AI features consume Databricks Units (DBUs). Vector Search is billed by index size (GB) and query throughput (DBUs per query). Model Serving is billed by compute instance hours or DBUs depending on serving tier. Foundation Model API calls are billed per token. Training and fine-tuning jobs consume cluster DBUs at standard rates.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search and Atlas AI
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables storing, indexing, and querying vector embeddings alongside operational data in Atlas collections, using the $vectorSearch aggregation pipeline stage. This allows semantic search, RAG pipelines, and recommendation systems without moving data to a separate vector store. Atlas integrates with embedding providers and LLM frameworks including LangChain, LlamaIndex, Hugging Face, and OpenAI. Atlas AI also includes queryable encryption, Atlas Search (full-text), and Atlas Stream Processing for real-time AI applications. The combination of vector, full-text, and operational queries in a single platform is a core differentiator.
databases.vector_search_notes: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search is a native, fully managed vector search capability built into Atlas. It uses an HNSW index (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) for approximate nearest neighbor search and supports cosine, Euclidean, and dot product similarity. Vector indexes are defined via Atlas Search index definitions and queries use the $vectorSearch aggregation stage. This is a native Atlas feature, not a third-party extension.
databases.llm_integration: Atlas integrates with external LLM providers via application frameworks rather than direct SQL-level LLM calls. First-class integrations exist with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, and Spring AI for building RAG pipelines. Atlas also supports direct API integration with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Vertex AI, and AWS Bedrock at the application layer. No native SQL-based LLM invocation function equivalent to Snowflake Cortex or BigQuery ML.GENERATE_TEXT.
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search requires an M10 or higher cluster tier (no free tier for vector search). Vector index storage counts toward Atlas storage billing. Query costs are included in cluster pricing rather than billed per query. Embedding generation costs are incurred externally via the chosen embedding provider API.
